name: Decision rights
short_description: Decision rights define who in an organization is allowed to make, approve and override which decisions; in cloud governance they are often captured in a decision rights matrix covering standards, security, funding, exceptions and lifecycle ownership.

evidence.quote: But behaviors didn't change. Decision rights didn't change. Accountability didn't change.
You have to move away from tribal knowledge and hidden coordination toward explicit decision rights.
That might mean moving decision rights closer to the work
First are decision rights which define who can actually make the call.
Decision rights stayed vague and approval chains stayed long
If your decision rights are unclear, it scales ambiguity.
Second, decision rights are explicit. Who can interpret policy, who can approve exceptions
